rationale_summary: The Opinion is overwhelmingly framed around fundamental_rights, as the EDPB interprets GDPR provisions to protect data subjects' EU Charter rights—specifically privacy (Article 7), personal data protection (Article 8), freedom of expression (Article 11), non-discrimination (Article 21), and self-determination—throughout AI model development and deployment. While innovation_enablement appears as a secondary rationale in the preamble and admissibility section (characterizing GDPR as a framework that supports AI opportunities and encourages responsible innovation through consistent supervisory application) and consumer_public_safety appears in the balancing test (citing risks of fraud, phishing, deepfakes, physical/mental harm, and manipulation of vulnerable individuals), both remain subordinate to the document's core legal mandate of safeguarding individual fundamental rights and freedoms.

evidence_spans.quote: By protecting the fundamental right to data protection, GDPR supports these opportunities and promotes other EU fundamental rights, including the right to freedom of thought, expression and information, the right to education or the freedom to conduct a business.

In relation to the fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subjects, the development and deployment of AI models may raise serious risks to rights protected by the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights (the “EU Charter”), including, but not limited to, the right to private and family life (Article 7 EU Charter) and the right to protection of personal data (Article 8 EU Charter).
Additionally, AI technologies create many opportunities and benefits across a wide range of sectors and social activities. Besides, GDPR is a legal framework that encourages responsible innovation.

deployment of AI models may also present risks to the security and safety of the individual (e.g. where the AI model is used with malicious intent), as well as risks to their physical and mental integrity

this may include controls limiting as much as possible their use for harmful practices, for instance: the creation of deepfakes; chatbots that are used for disinformation, phishing and other types of fraud; and manipulative AI/AI agents
